education.headline: Dry, gritty eyes after a day at the *screen?*
education.body: Blink more, look 20 feet away every 20 minutes, and ask us about dry eye therapy if drops stop helping.
education.chip: Ask us at your next visit

education.headline: Night driving getting *harder?*
education.body: Halos around headlights and faded colors are common early signs of a cloudy lens (cataract). A dilated exam will tell you where you stand.

cover.headline: What happens at a cataract *consult*
cover.body: Four steps, one visit. Swipe through.

slides.headline: A dilated exam
slides.body: Drops widen your pupils so the doctor can see the lens and the retina behind it. Plan for blurry near vision for a few hours afterward.

slides.headline: Measurements of your eye
slides.body: Painless scans measure the length and curve of your eye. They decide the power of the replacement lens.

slides.headline: Choosing a lens
slides.body: Standard, toric for astigmatism, or a light adjustable lens that is fine-tuned after surgery. We go through the options with you.

slides.headline: Booking the surgery
slides.body: Surgery takes place at an outpatient surgery center, not in the office, one eye at a time. Most people go home the same morning.
